title: For EU Markets: Removal of approved couriers for Shipped by Seller (3PL) domestic orders
breadcrumb: For EU Markets: Removal of approved couriers for Shipped by Seller (3PL) domestic orders
label: TIKTOK SHOP · CHANGELOG
subtitle: Updated 2026-10-08
html:
What is changing?

TikTok Shop periodically reviews the couriers approved for the Shipped by Seller (3PL) fulfillment method. Effective October 14, 2026, the couriers listed below will be removed from the approved courier list for domestic EU orders. This change applies to local-to-local (L2L) sellers only.

Which markets are affected?

This change affects domestic orders in Spain (ES), Italy (IT), France (FR), and Germany (DE). The scope is L2L only.

Who is affected?

This change affects developers and applications that support sellers using Shipped by Seller (3PL) for domestic orders in ES, IT, FR, and DE, where those integrations use or maintain approved courier selections for L2L workflows.

What action is required?

  1. Update your applications. Use the most current shipping provider IDs returned by the Get Shipping Providers endpoint. This endpoint should be called dynamically as some sellers may be whitelisted and still have access to removed provider ids.
  2. Inform your seller base. Notify sellers of this change and the available options below to help them avoid order sync issues.
  3. Ask sellers to choose one of the following options:
    • Option A — Switch to an approved courier. Sellers must switch to an approved courier before October 14, 2026 to avoid order cancellations. See the approved courier list.
    • Option B — Switch to Shipped via Platform. TikTok provides shipping labels in Seller Center and updates tracking information automatically. Read the Shipped via Platform guidance.
    • Option C — Switch to Fulfilled by TikTok. TikTok stores, packs, and ships sellers’ orders.
  4. No action is required for existing tracking numbers. Tracking numbers updated before October 14, 2026 will continue to be tracked normally after that date.
